descriptions.before: Describes whether a ContextAction should sink or pass input events.
descriptions.after: Describes whether a contextual action should sink or pass input events.

descriptions.before: If functionToBind from ContextActionService:BindAction() returns Enum.ContextActionResult.Sink, the input event will stop at that function and no other bound actions under it will be processed. This is the default behavior if functionToBind does not return anything or yields in any way.
descriptions.after: If functionToBind from ContextActionService:BindAction() returns ContextActionResult.Sink, the input event will stop at that function and no other bound actions under it will be processed. This is the default behavior if functionToBind does not return anything or yields in any way.

descriptions.before: If functionToBind from ContextActionService:BindAction() returns Enum.ContextActionResult.Pass, the input event is considered to have not been handled by functionToBind and will continue being passed to actions bound to the same input type.
descriptions.after: If functionToBind from ContextActionService:BindAction() returns ContextActionResult.Pass, the input event is considered to have not been handled by functionToBind and will continue being passed to actions bound to the same input type.

descriptions.before: The player's character will moved based on the user's settings.
descriptions.after: Allows players to choose their desired control scheme from the in-experience menu. This is the default movement mode.

descriptions.before: The player can right click in the game world and the character will move there. Player can also control character with mouse and keyboard.
descriptions.after: Players can only move through the experience by clicking a target location. The player's character will automatically jump when reaching a surmountable obstacle/gap while moving to the click destination.

descriptions.before: The player will not respond to default controls. You must define any character movement in custom scripts.
descriptions.after: Disables all default controls and allows you to script your own control scheme.

descriptions.before: Overrides the movement mode of players who are playing on touch devices.
descriptions.after: Overrides the movement mode of players who are playing on touch-enabled devices.

descriptions.before: The player's character will moved based on the user's settings.
descriptions.after: Allows players to choose their desired control scheme from the in-experience menu. This is the default movement mode.

descriptions.before: The player will not respond to default controls; any character movement must be defined in custom scripts.
descriptions.after: The player's character will not respond to default controls; any character movement must be defined in custom scripts.

descriptions.before: The player's character is controlled with a virtual thumbstick that appears when they touch the lower portion of the screen. Jumping is controlled with a separate button. Good for portrait mode and one handed play.
descriptions.after: The player's character is controlled with a virtual thumbstick that appears when they touch the lower portion of the screen. Jumping is controlled with a separate button.

descriptions.before: The InputAction will receive boolean values from button inputs, for example true/false on press/release from inputs such as KeyCode.ButtonA or KeyCode.E.
descriptions.after: The InputAction will receive boolean values from button inputs, for example true/false on press/release from inputs such as KeyCode.ButtonA or KeyCode.E. This setting also exposes the UIButton property on child InputBindings, allowing you to easily hook up press or release of a GuiButton for the action.

descriptions.before: The InputAction will receive numerical values, generally from analog gamepad triggers such as KeyCode.ButtonL2 or KeyCode.ButtonR2.
descriptions.after: The InputAction will receive numerical values, generally from analog gamepad triggers such as KeyCode.ButtonL2 or KeyCode.ButtonR2. This setting also exposes the Up and Down properties on child InputBindings, allowing for boolean inputs or "1D" inputs as composite directions for the action.

descriptions.before: The InputAction will receive Vector2 values, generally from thumbstick inputs such as KeyCode.Thumbstick1 and KeyCode.Thumbstick2.
descriptions.after: The InputAction will receive Vector2 values, generally from thumbstick inputs such as KeyCode.Thumbstick1 and KeyCode.Thumbstick2. This setting also exposes the Up, Down, Left, and Right properties on child InputBindings, allowing for "2D" inputs as composite directions for the action.

The InputAction will receive Vector3 values from inputs assigned to the Up, Down, Left, Right, Forward, and/or Backward properties on child InputBindings, allowing for "3D" inputs as composite directions for the action.
This enum is used with UserInputService.PreferredInput to indicate the primary input type a player is likely using.
The player has connected or most recently interacted with a keyboard or mouse.
The player has connected or most recently interacted with a gamepad.
The player's device has touch capability and no other input method is available or connected.

descriptions.before: The UserInputState enum describes the state of an input that is currently or was recently performed.
descriptions.after: This enum describes the state of an input that is currently or was recently performed.

descriptions.before: Occurs when an InputObject starts to interact with the game. For example, a mouse button down, or a key down, or when a touch begins touching the screen.
descriptions.after: Occurs when an InputObject starts to interact with the experience. For example, a mouse button down, a key down, or when the player begins touching the screen.

descriptions.before: Occurs each frame an InputObject has already begun interacting with the game and part of its state is changing. For example, a movement of the mouse position, a gamepad thumbstick, gamepad trigger button, or screen touch point.
descriptions.after: Occurs each frame an InputObject has already begun interacting with the experience and part of its state is changing. For example, movement of the mouse position, a gamepad thumbstick movement, an analog gamepad trigger button change, or screen touch point change.

descriptions.before: When an InputObject finishes interacting with the game. For example, a mouse button up, or a key up, or when a touch stops touching the screen.
descriptions.after: Occurs when an InputObject finishes interacting with the experience. For example, a mouse button up, a key up, or when the player stops touching the screen.

descriptions.before: A special circumstance state that indicates this input is no longer relevant, particularly with ContextActionService. For example, binding two action-handling functions will cause the first to Cancel if an input was already in-progress when the second was bound.
descriptions.after: A special circumstance state that indicates this input is no longer relevant, particularly with ContextActionService. For example, binding two action-handling functions will cause the first to Cancel if an input was already in-progress when the second was bound.

descriptions.before: A state that should never be seen in a game, essentially just marks the end of the enum.
descriptions.after: A state that should never be seen in an experience; essentially just marks the end of the enum.
